raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Since #44455 (KV-cache layout refactor, v0.26), `FlashAttentionImpl` re-derives
the K/V cache views on **every** attention call: in `forward` it runs
`kv_cache.transpose(1, 2).split(head_size, dim=-1)` and then
`canonicalize_singleton_dim_strides` on both views, and in `do_kv_cache_update`
it runs the same `transpose(1, 2).split(...)`. Before #44455 this was a single
`kv_cache.unbind(1)`.

These views depend only on the per-layer `kv_cache` tensor's storage, shape and
strides, all of which are fixed once the KV cache is allocated. Under the
default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, attention for prefill / mixed batches runs
eagerly, so this derivation is host time on the critical path for short
prefills. The issue (#59534) measures ~+21 µs per `unified_attention_with_output`
call on H100 (K/V view ops 11.6 µs → 17.0 µs), ~+1.35 ms per prefill step for a
64-layer model, and a 1–3.5 ms TTFT p50 regression on 8×H100 (TP=8) with short
prompts and `max_tokens=1`. Only the FA backend is affected; FlashInfer is not.

Fixes #59534.

## Claims

- The derived K/V views are now computed once per `kv_cache` tensor and reused
  on subsequent calls, removing the per-call `transpose`/`split`/canonicalize
  host work from the FA critical path.
- Output is unchanged: the cached views are byte-identical to the derivation
  they replace (same shape, strides and values).
- The cache is keyed on the `kv_cache` tensor **identity**, so it is rebuilt
  when the tensor is replaced — in particular the profiling path that binds a
  minimal KV cache, runs attention, frees it, then allocates the real cache
  never sees stale views pointing at freed memory.

## Implementation

A single `FlashAttentionImpl._get_kv_views(kv_cache, canonicalize)` helper
derives and caches the views. It caches both variants from one derivation:
`forward` needs the canonicalized views (TMA requires ≥16-byte strides on
size-1 dims), while `do_kv_cache_update` writes with a scatter op that needs no
canonicalization. The cache (`self._kv_view_cache`) is a per-impl tuple
`(kv_cache, key_raw, value_raw, key_canon, value_canon)`; the `is` identity
check rebuilds it on tensor replacement.

This mirrors existing precedent: `TritonAttentionImpl` already caches its KV
scale views in `_k_scale_cache` / `_v_scale_cache`.

Profiling memory: `_cleanup_profiling_kv_cache` frees the minimal profiling KV
cache, and holding cached views of it would keep its storage alive. The cleanup
already clears the Triton scale caches for exactly this reason, so this PR
clears `_kv_view_cache` in the same place; the identity check covers any
remaining replacement path.

## Validation

All validation ran on an RTX 5090 (CUDA, sm_120), vLLM at
`main @ 4e0ad5720` with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` editable install,
torch 2.14.0+cu132, Ubuntu 24.04.

**Fails before / passes after.** The regression test pins the new helper's
contract (views byte-identical to the derivation they replace, reused on the
same tensor, rebuilt on identity change). On the base commit the helper does
not exist, so all four tests fail:

```text
# base commit
$ pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_flash_attn_kv_view_cache.py
E       AttributeError: 'FlashAttentionImpl' object has no attribute '_get_kv_views'
FAILED ...::test_views_match_reference
FAILED ...::test_same_tensor_reuses_cached_views
FAILED ...::test_new_tensor_rebuilds_views
FAILED ...::test_single_kv_head_raw_and_canonicalized_variants
4 failed in 13.62s

# with this PR
$ pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_flash_attn_kv_view_cache.py
4 passed in 3.37s
```

**Output unchanged** — existing FA correctness suites:

```text
$ pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_mm_prefix.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_kv_head_stride_canonicalization.py
4 failed, 173 passed, 28 skipped in 761.67s (0:12:41)
```

The 4 failures are all
`test_sliding_window_encoder_backend_correctness[*-google/embeddinggemma-300m-*]`
failing with HTTP 401 (gated HF checkpoint, no token on the box). Verified the
same test fails identically on the base commit — environmental, unrelated to
this change.

**Microbench** — host time per call (N=2000 iters after warmup, bf16 cache,
blocks=1000 / block_size=16 / head_size=128):

| per-call host cost | kv_heads=1 | =4 | =8 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| base `forward` derivation (`transpose+split+2x canonicalize`) | 10.66 µs | 6.04 µs | 5.84 µs |
| base `do_kv_cache_update` derivation (`transpose+split`) | 5.40 µs | 5.46 µs | 5.22 µs |
| **with fix: `_get_kv_views` cache hit** | **0.12 µs** | **0.13 µs** | **0.12 µs** |

I.e. ~5.7–10.5 µs saved per forward call and ~5.1–5.3 µs per KV-update call,
per layer per eager step, consistent with the ~+21 µs/call profiler delta
reported in #59534 on H100 (both call sites plus surrounding ops).

**pre-commit** — all applicable hooks passed on the three changed files
(ruff, format, mypy, SPDX, forbidden-imports, Buildkite test wiring, etc.),
0 failed:

```text
$ pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_flash_attn_kv_view_cache.py \
    vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py
Failed count: 0  (incl. "Check new tests are wired into Buildkite CI": Passed —
the new test lives in tests/v1/attention/, already selected by
.buildkite/test_areas/attention.yaml)
```

## Follow-up

The same per-call derivation exists in other eager-path backends
(line numbers @ `65ff14056`): `triton_attn.py` (L655/744/828/863, where the
FP8-KV path additionally re-runs two `view(fp8_dtype)` retypes per call —
measured 6.97–7.23 µs/call on the same box), `flex_attention.py` (L1233/1346),
`hpc_attn.py` (L443), `rocm_aiter_fa.py` (L1666), `flash_attn_diffkv.py`
(L111/193), and the trtllm path in `flashinfer.py` (L2839/2844).
`TritonAttentionImpl` already caches its KV *scale* views the same way. If this
approach lands, I'm happy to extend the caching to those backends in follow-up
PRs.

## Why this is not a duplicate

No open PR addresses the per-call K/V view derivation in `FlashAttentionImpl`.
Searched open PRs for `59534`, `_get_kv_views`, and FA `transpose(1, 2).split`
view caching — none found. The related view-caching precedent in
`TritonAttentionImpl` is existing code, not an open PR.

## Pull Request Checklist

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

This only clears `_kv_view_cache` in V1's `_cleanup_profiling_kv_cache`. Model Runner V2 is the default, and its profiling teardown and `shutdown()` both go through `clear_layer_kv_caches` in `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py`, which only resets the scale caches. Moving the reset into `clear_layer_kv_caches` next to the scale caches would cover both paths.

You're right on all three points: `use_v2_model_runner` defaults to true, MRV2's teardown paths go through `clear_layer_kv_caches` (`gpu/model_runner.py` profiling teardown + `shutdown()`, and `gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`), and that helper only reset the scale caches — so the cached views kept the detached `kv_cache` tensor alive exactly as you describe.

The fix resets `_kv_view_cache` in `clear_layer_kv_caches` next to the scale caches. I kept the V1 inline reset in `_cleanup_profiling_kv_cache` as well, since V1 doesn't call the shared helper — it inlines the same pattern (the scale-cache resets are already duplicated the same way in both places), so the two stay symmetric. Also added a regression test that exercises the shared helper against a real `FlashAttentionImpl` with a populated view cache.

detail.title: [Perf][Attention] Cache FlashAttention K/V cache views per tensor

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,168 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""FlashAttentionImpl K/V view caching (issue #59534).
+
+Since #44455 ``FlashAttentionImpl`` re-derived the K/V cache views
+(``transpose(1, 2).split(head_size)`` plus stride canonicalization) on every
+attention call, even though the views depend only on the ``kv_cache`` tensor's
+storage/shape/strides, which are fixed once the cache is allocated. The views
+are now cached on the impl and reused while the same ``kv_cache`` tensor is
+passed in.
+
+This optimization must not change the views it returns, so the tests compare
+the cached views against the exact derivation they replace. They also assert
+the cache is actually reused (same tensor -> identical view objects) and is
+rebuilt on identity change (the profiling path binds a minimal KV cache, frees
+it, then allocates the real one).
+
+The impl constructor probes the platform for the FlashAttention version, so the
+tests require CUDA with FlashAttention available.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config import set_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+
+def _fa_available() -> bool:
+    if not current_platform.is_cuda():
+        return False
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.fa_utils import is_fa_version_supported
+
+    return is_fa_version_supported(3) or is_fa_version_supported(2)
+
+
+requires_fa = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not _fa_available(), reason="FlashAttentionImpl requires CUDA with FlashAttention"
+)
+
+if _fa_available():
+    from tests.v1.attention.utils import create_vllm_config
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.flash_attn import FlashAttentionImpl
+
+HEAD_SIZE = 128
+BLOCK_SIZE = 16
+NUM_BLOCKS = 8
+
+
+def _make_impl(num_kv_heads: int) -> "FlashAttentionImpl":
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(block_size=BLOCK_SIZE)
+    with set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config):
+        return FlashAttentionImpl(
+            num_heads=num_kv_heads,
+            head_size=HEAD_SIZE,
+            scale=1.0 / (HEAD_SIZE**0.5),
+            num_kv_heads=num_kv_heads,
+            alibi_slopes=None,
+            sliding_window=None,
+            kv_cache_dtype="auto",
+        )
+
+
+def _make_kv_cache(num_kv_heads: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # FA packed layout: (B, H, N, 2*D); forward does transpose(1, 2).split(D).
+    return torch.randn(
+        NUM_BLOCKS,
+        num_kv_heads,
+        BLOCK_SIZE,
+        2 * HEAD_SIZE,
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        device="cuda",
+    )
+
+
+def _reference_views(kv_cache: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    # The derivation _get_kv_views replaces.
+    return kv_cache.transpose(1, 2).split(HEAD_SIZE, dim=-1)
+
+
+@requires_fa
+class TestFlashAttentionKVViewCache:
+    def test_views_match_reference(self):
+        """Cached views are identical to the derivation they replace."""
+        impl = _make_impl(num_kv_heads=4)
+        kv_cache = _make_kv_cache(num_kv_heads=4)
+        k_ref, v_ref = _reference_views(kv_cache)
+
+        k, v = impl._get_kv_views(kv_cache, canonicalize=False)
+
+        # num_kv_heads > 1 has canonical strides, so raw == canonicalized here.
+        assert k.shape == k_ref.shape and v.shape == v_ref.shape
+        assert k.stride() == k_ref.stride() and v.stride() == v_ref.stride()
+        assert torch.equal(k, k_ref) and torch.equal(v, v_ref)
+
+    def test_same_tensor_reuses_cached_views(self):
+        """Passing the same kv_cache returns the identical view objects."""
+        impl = _make_impl(num_kv_heads=4)
+        kv_cache = _make_kv_cache(num_kv_heads=4)
+
+        k1, v1 = impl._get_kv_views(kv_cache, canonicalize=True)
+        k2, v2 = impl._get_kv_views(kv_cache, canonicalize=True)
+        assert k2 is k1 and v2 is v1
+
+        # The raw (uncanonicalized) variant is served from the same cache entry.
+        k_raw1, v_raw1 = impl._get_kv_views(kv_cache, canonicalize=False)
+        k_raw2, v_raw2 = impl._get_kv_views(kv_cache, canonicalize=False)
+        assert k_raw2 is k_raw1 and v_raw2 is v_raw1
+
+    def test_new_tensor_rebuilds_views(self):
+        """A different kv_cache tensor rebuilds the views (profiling path)."""
+        impl = _make_impl(num_kv_heads=4)
+        first = _make_kv_cache(num_kv_heads=4)
+        second = _make_kv_cache(num_kv_heads=4)
+
+        k_first, _ = impl._get_kv_views(first, canonicalize=False)
+        k_second, _ = impl._get_kv_views(second, canonicalize=False)
+
+        assert k_second is not k_first
+        k_ref, _ = _reference_views(second)
+        assert torch.equal(k_second, k_ref)
+
+    def test_clear_layer_kv_caches_drops_view_cache(self):
+        """Runner teardown must drop the cached views, or the detached
+        kv_cache tensor stays alive through them.
+
+        Both runners release layer KV caches on profiling teardown and
+        shutdown: Model Runner V2 (and the cudagraph utils) via
+        clear_layer_kv_caches, V1 via the same pattern inlined in
+        _cleanup_profiling_kv_cache.
+        """
+        from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+        from vllm.v1.worker.utils import clear_layer_kv_caches
+
+        impl = _make_impl(num_kv_heads=4)
+        kv_cache = _make_kv_cache(num_kv_heads=4)
+        impl._get_kv_views(kv_cache, canonicalize=True)
+        assert impl._kv_view_cache is not None
+
+        layer = SimpleNamespace(kv_cache=kv_cache, impl=impl)
+        clear_layer_kv_caches([layer])
+
+        assert impl._kv_view_cache is None
+        assert layer.kv_cache.numel() == 0
+
+    def test_single_kv_head_raw_and_canonicalized_variants(self):
+        """With one KV head the two variants share storage and values; the
+        canonicalized view carries canonical size-1 strides.
+
+        (The degenerate-stride *repair* itself is covered by the
+        canonicalize_singleton_dim_strides unit tests; a freshly allocated
+        contiguous cache is already canonical, so here the two variants agree.)
+        """
+        impl = _make_impl(num_kv_heads=1)
+        kv_cache = _make_kv_cache(num_kv_heads=1)
+
+        # After transpose(1, 2) the size-1 KV-head dim is -2; its canonical
+        # stride is head_size.
+        k_raw, v_raw = impl._get_kv_views(kv_cache, canonicalize=False)
+        k_canon, v_canon = impl._get_kv_views(kv_cache, canonicalize=True)
+
+        assert k_canon.stride(-2) == HEAD_SIZE and v_canon.stride(-2) == HEAD_SIZE
+        # Same storage, zero-copy.

inline_comments.body: This only clears `_kv_view_cache` in V1's `_cleanup_profiling_kv_cache`. Model Runner V2 is the default, and its profiling teardown and `shutdown()` both go through `clear_layer_kv_caches` in `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py`, which only resets the scale caches. So on MRV2 each FlashAttentionImpl keeps the profiling KV tensor alive in `_kv_view_cache[0]` until the first real forward, and after shutdown it pins the real KV cache whenever the model outlives the runner. Moving the reset into `clear_layer_kv_caches` next to the scale caches would cover both paths.

Good catch, thank you — confirmed and fixed in e86d17be5.

You're right on all three points: `use_v2_model_runner` defaults to true, MRV2's teardown paths go through `clear_layer_kv_caches` (`gpu/model_runner.py` profiling teardown + `shutdown()`, and `gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`), and that helper only reset the scale caches — so the cached views kept the detached `kv_cache` tensor alive exactly as you describe.

The fix resets `_kv_view_cache` in `clear_layer_kv_caches` next to the scale caches. I kept the V1 inline reset in `_cleanup_profiling_kv_cache` as well, since V1 doesn't call the shared helper — it inlines the same pattern (the scale-cache resets are already duplicated the same way in both places), so the two stay symmetric. Also added a regression test that exercises the shared helper against a real `FlashAttentionImpl` with a populated view cache.

Validation on an NVIDIA L4 (sm_89): `tests/v1/attention/test_flash_attn_kv_view_cache.py` — 5 passed (including the new `test_clear_layer_kv_caches_drops_view_cache`), and `pre-commit` on both changed files — 0 failed.
